title: Microeconomic Theory
summary: This document is a comprehensive textbook on microeconomic theory, covering topics such as individual decision making, game theory, market equilibrium, and general equilibrium. It provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for analyzing consumer choice, production, market power, and information economics.

title: Lecture Notes in Microeconomic Theory: The Economic Agent
summary: This document provides lecture notes for a graduate-level microeconomics course, focusing on the behavior of individual economic agents. It covers topics such as preferences, utility, consumer choice, risk aversion, and social choice, while emphasizing the interpretation of economic models as 'fables' rather than absolute truths.

title: Economics and Language: Five Essays
summary: This book explores the intersection of economic theory and linguistics through five essays. It examines how economic modeling can explain the structure and evolution of natural language, as well as how language and rhetoric influence economic theory and decision-making.

title: Modeling Bounded Rationality
summary: This book explores theoretical frameworks for modeling bounded rationality in economics, focusing on procedural decision-making rather than traditional perfect rationality. It covers topics such as limited memory, knowledge structures, complexity in group decisions, and computability constraints in game theory.

title: Models in Microeconomic Theory
summary: This textbook provides an introduction to intermediate microeconomic theory, focusing on the concepts of models and equilibrium. It covers individual behavior, market equilibrium, game theory, and various economic topics such as mechanism design and social choice.

title: Preference Relations and Choice Theory
summary: This document outlines the fundamental properties of preference relations, including completeness and transitivity, and their role in defining choice sets. It further explores the conditions under which choice correspondences can be represented by utility functions and provides a proof sketch for utility representation on finite sets.

title: Utility Maximization and Choice Theory
summary: This document outlines the theoretical foundations of utility maximization, focusing on choice correspondences and preference relations. It details the axiomatic requirements for rational choice, including WARP, Axiom alpha, and Axiom beta, while discussing the limitations of these models in behavioral contexts.

title: Microeconomic Analysis Homework 1
summary: This document contains a problem set for a microeconomic analysis course, focusing on choice theory. It covers topics such as choice correspondences, WARP (Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference), utility maximization, satisficing, and choice with consideration sets.

title: Microeconomic Analysis Homework 2
summary: This document contains a set of advanced microeconomic theory problems focusing on utility representation theorems, preference relations, and choice process models. It explores the implications of various data set constraints on choice behavior and the mathematical foundations of utility functions.

title: Microeconomic Analysis Homework 1 Solutions
summary: This document contains detailed solutions to a Microeconomic Analysis homework assignment covering choice theory, specifically choice correspondences, axioms of revealed preference (WARP, alpha, beta), and models of choice with consideration sets. It provides proofs and counterexamples for various decision-making procedures and their consistency with rational choice axioms.

title: Microeconomic Analysis 1: Choice Theory Introduction
summary: This document provides an introductory overview of choice theory and utility maximization within a microeconomics course. It explains how to test for utility maximization using choice data and introduces the Independence of Irrelevant Alternatives (IIA) as a necessary condition for rational behavior.

title: Preferences, Utility and Choice
summary: These lecture notes introduce the fundamental concepts of utility maximization, choice correspondences, and preference relations in microeconomic theory. The document outlines the representation theorem, which establishes the necessary and sufficient conditions (Axioms alpha and beta) for data to be consistent with utility maximization.

title: Utility Maximization: Extensions to Non-Finite Sets
summary: This document explores the limitations of utility representation theorems when moving from finite to infinite choice sets. It introduces concepts such as lexicographic preferences, order separability, continuity, and the Hausdorff metric to establish conditions under which utility functions can represent preferences in non-finite domains.

title: A Representation Theorem for Utility Maximization: Proofs
summary: These notes provide a step-by-step proof demonstrating the equivalence between choice axioms (alpha and beta) and preference maximization, as well as the existence of a utility function for finite sets. The document outlines the logical progression from observed choices to binary relations and finally to utility representation using inductive reasoning.

title: GR6211: Microeconomic Analysis I Syllabus
summary: This document is the course syllabus for a PhD-level microeconomics course at Columbia University. It outlines the course structure, assessment criteria, recommended readings, and the specific topics covered in the first half of the sequence, which focuses on choice theory.

title: GR6211: Microeconomic Analysis I Syllabus
summary: This document is the course syllabus for a PhD-level microeconomics course at Columbia University. It outlines the course structure, assessment policies, recommended readings, and a detailed topical breakdown of choice theory, demand functions, producer theory, and decision-making under risk and time.

title: The Representation Theorem and Utility Theory
summary: This document explores the mathematical foundations of utility theory, focusing on the representation theorem and the axioms of revealed preference (WARP). It discusses the ordinal nature of utility functions, the challenges posed by infinite choice sets, and the conditions for utility representation such as order separability and continuity.

title: Microeconomics: Choice Theory and Utility Maximization
summary: This document explores the foundational model of utility maximization in microeconomics and how to test it against observed choice data. It contrasts two approaches to testing—assuming a specific utility metric versus an 'as if' approach—and introduces the Independence of Irrelevant Alternatives (IIA) as a necessary condition for consistent utility-maximizing behavior.

title: Necessity and Sufficiency of IIA for Utility Functions
summary: This document examines whether the Independence of Irrelevant Alternatives (IIA) is a necessary and sufficient condition for rationalizing choice data with a utility function. It explains that while IIA is necessary for utility maximization, it is not sufficient on its own, requiring additional conditions like Axiom beta to guarantee rationalizability.

title: Microeconomics: Utility Maximization and Preference Relations
summary: This document explores the formal representation of consumer choice through utility maximization and preference relations. It covers the definition of choice correspondences, the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference (WARP), and the properties of binary relations such as completeness and transitivity.

title: Why Reflexivity is Implied by Completeness
summary: This document explains why reflexivity is not required as an independent axiom for preference relations in microeconomic theory. It demonstrates that reflexivity is logically guaranteed by the definition of completeness when applied to an alternative compared against itself.

title: Microeconomics: Preference Relations and Utility Representation
summary: This document explores the formal properties of preference relations, including completeness and transitivity, and their role in modeling choice behavior. It details the proof that a choice correspondence satisfies axioms alpha and beta if and only if it can be represented by a preference relation, and further demonstrates how such preferences can be represented by a utility function using mathematical induction.

title: Utility Representation Theorems and Preference Continuity
summary: This document explores the conditions under which choice correspondences and preference relations can be represented by utility functions. It covers the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference (WARP), the role of finiteness and countability in utility representation, and the importance of order separability and continuity in defining preferences on metric spaces.

title: The Role of Unfalsifiable Axioms in Economic Modeling
summary: This document explores why economists utilize 'Class 3' axioms, such as continuity, which cannot be directly falsified by finite empirical data. It explains that these axioms are essential for mathematical tractability, ensuring the existence of utility-maximizing solutions, and enabling the derivation of testable predictions like Slutsky symmetry.

title: Microeconomics: Utility Representation and Revealed Preference
summary: This document explores the mathematical foundations of utility representation, covering Debreu's Theorem and the construction of utility functions for continuous preference relations. It further discusses choice theory, the Hausdorff metric for choice correspondences, and the Generalized Axiom of Revealed Preference (GARP) as a framework for rationalizing observed consumer behavior.

title: Microeconomic Choice Theory and Rationalization
summary: This document explores the theoretical foundations of choice theory, specifically addressing how to rationalize choice correspondences when the choice set is infinite or when observations are incomplete. It covers the role of compactness, continuity, and revealed preference axioms (SARP/GARP) in ensuring the existence of a utility function representation.

title: Microeconomics: Choice Theory and Utility Maximization
summary: This document explores the foundations of choice theory and the utility maximization model in microeconomics. It discusses methodological approaches to testing rational behavior, the consistency of preferences, and the role of the Independence of Irrelevant Alternatives (IIA) axiom.

title: Utility Maximization 3: Random Utility
summary: These lecture notes introduce the concept of Random Utility Models (RUM) as a way to model stochastic choice behavior in microeconomics. The document covers the formal definition of RUM, necessary conditions for rationalizability such as the Block-Marschak inequalities and the Axiom of Revealed Stochastic Preference, and concludes with an overview of the Luce model.

title: Failures of Utility Maximization
summary: This document outlines various empirical violations of the standard utility maximization model in economics, including violations of the Independence of Irrelevant Alternatives (IIA) and the endowment effect. It reviews classic behavioral experiments such as the jam study by Iyengar and Lepper, the compromise effect, and preference reversals to illustrate how human decision-making often deviates from rational choice theory.

title: Microeconomic Analysis Homework 4
summary: This document contains a problem set for a microeconomic analysis course, focusing on random choice models, utility functions, and consumer theory. It covers topics such as consideration sets, preference axioms, demand correspondences, and the limitations of the representative consumer model.
